# requireNonNumber

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonNumber() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonNumber<T>(
  value: T | number,
  message: string = "Expected a non-numeric value."
): T;
```

The test is `typeof value === "number"`, which `NaN` and both infinities satisfy. Use `isFloat`, `isInteger` or `isNaN` when those cases have to be told apart.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                  | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                    | `T \| number` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-numeric value."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a number excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition              |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a number. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonNumber("1"); // => "1"
requireNonNumber(null); // => null
requireNonNumber(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonNumber(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
